sections.title: The image does not say whose heart this is
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A red heart floats against a grey background, pierced by three swords. The middle blade is almost vertical; the others cross at angles. Low clouds gather above and at the sides, with long fine lines of rain below. There are no people, buildings or conversations to identify the heart’s owner.

The red heart contrasts strongly with the cool blades, giving the eye little room to look away. The hurt is explicit, but its cause is not shown. Three swords can invite us to consider several contributing factors; they do not establish that a “third person” must be involved. [View the image examined for this article](https://github.com/guangtoulee/destinypixel/blob/284f7641e41dcaa6685d2d387e31245ca8264d66/public/tarot/rws/three-of-swords.webp)

sections.title: Waite writes about separation and rupture
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Waite’s transcription labelled 1911 lists departure, absence, delay, division and rupture, and treats the design as largely self-explanatory. His reversed list also includes error, loss and confusion. It does not support reading every reversal as a wound already healed.

This article uses the card to acknowledge disappointment and identify needs, a modern reflective approach. We retain the image’s gravity without applying the old list’s pathologising language to anyone’s mental state. [Check Waite’s original entry](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktsw03.htm)

sections.title: Upright: Connect the feeling to something specific
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Upright, the card can indicate a disappointed expectation or an acknowledgment that an arrangement falls short of your needs. Make “this feels awful” more precise: were you left uninformed, misunderstood, or faced with a changed agreement? Naming it helps you choose what to do next.

Acknowledging hurt does not require immediate forgiveness or an immediate end to a relationship. The facts, their impact and your needs can be addressed separately. Some things can be renegotiated; some losses take time to accept.

sections.title: Reversed: Notice how the hurt is being handled
sections.bodyMarkdown: Reversed, the card can suggest willingness to discuss a painful point, or repeatedly replaying the same words without an opportunity to clarify them. Notice whether your choices are returning or you are forcing yourself to move on quickly. It cannot establish that another person regrets their actions; repair depends on real responses and change.

sections.title: Disappointment is not limited to romance
sections.bodyMarkdown:
After a rejected proposal, distinguish feedback on the work from a judgment on your whole self. Ask whether the objection concerned the budget, direction or presentation. A vague setback can then become something more workable.

If a friend cancels a long-awaited meeting, say that you are disappointed and ask whether you will reschedule. Hurtful words in a relationship call for a specific conversation about their impact, not a card used as an accusation. Leaving a familiar city can bring sadness alongside a wish to try a new life.

sections.title: Practice: Write a message you do not send yet
sections.bodyMarkdown: Write three sentences to the person or situation that disappointed you: “What happened”; “What I lost because of it”; “What I need now.” Set it aside briefly, then check whether you have stated an unverified motive as fact. You can decide later whether to communicate it.

sections.title: Three swords are not evidence of a love triangle
sections.bodyMarkdown: The Three of Swords cannot prove betrayal or guarantee a breakup. Pain deserves serious attention, but a card cannot replace people’s own accounts, reliable evidence or genuine negotiation.

articleMarkdown:
# Three of Swords Meaning: Give Disappointment an Accurate Name

In one sentence: Acknowledge what hurts before deciding what needs expressing, repairing or letting go.

Keywords: Disappointment · Separation · Acknowledgment

Upright at a glance: Recognise the hurt and disagreement, and face what has actually happened.

Reversed at a glance: The hurt may still be tangled, or you may be finding ways to express it and loosen its hold.

A sentence has stayed with you and hurt for a long time. “I’m fine” may not be what needs saying.

## The image does not say whose heart this is

A red heart floats against a grey background, pierced by three swords. The middle blade is almost vertical; the others cross at angles. Low clouds gather above and at the sides, with long fine lines of rain below. There are no people, buildings or conversations to identify the heart’s owner.

The red heart contrasts strongly with the cool blades, giving the eye little room to look away. The hurt is explicit, but its cause is not shown. Three swords can invite us to consider several contributing factors; they do not establish that a “third person” must be involved. [View the image examined for this article](https://github.com/guangtoulee/destinypixel/blob/284f7641e41dcaa6685d2d387e31245ca8264d66/public/tarot/rws/three-of-swords.webp)

## Waite writes about separation and rupture

Waite’s transcription labelled 1911 lists departure, absence, delay, division and rupture, and treats the design as largely self-explanatory. His reversed list also includes error, loss and confusion. It does not support reading every reversal as a wound already healed.

This article uses the card to acknowledge disappointment and identify needs, a modern reflective approach. We retain the image’s gravity without applying the old list’s pathologising language to anyone’s mental state. [Check Waite’s original entry](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktsw03.htm)

## Upright: Connect the feeling to something specific

Upright, the card can indicate a disappointed expectation or an acknowledgment that an arrangement falls short of your needs. Make “this feels awful” more precise: were you left uninformed, misunderstood, or faced with a changed agreement? Naming it helps you choose what to do next.

Acknowledging hurt does not require immediate forgiveness or an immediate end to a relationship. The facts, their impact and your needs can be addressed separately. Some things can be renegotiated; some losses take time to accept.

## Reversed: Notice how the hurt is being handled

Reversed, the card can suggest willingness to discuss a painful point, or repeatedly replaying the same words without an opportunity to clarify them. Notice whether your choices are returning or you are forcing yourself to move on quickly. It cannot establish that another person regrets their actions; repair depends on real responses and change.

## Disappointment is not limited to romance

After a rejected proposal, distinguish feedback on the work from a judgment on your whole self. Ask whether the objection concerned the budget, direction or presentation. A vague setback can then become something more workable.

If a friend cancels a long-awaited meeting, say that you are disappointed and ask whether you will reschedule. Hurtful words in a relationship call for a specific conversation about their impact, not a card used as an accusation. Leaving a familiar city can bring sadness alongside a wish to try a new life.

## Practice: Write a message you do not send yet

Write three sentences to the person or situation that disappointed you: “What happened”; “What I lost because of it”; “What I need now.” Set it aside briefly, then check whether you have stated an unverified motive as fact. You can decide later whether to communicate it.

## Three swords are not evidence of a love triangle

The Three of Swords cannot prove betrayal or guarantee a breakup. Pain deserves serious attention, but a card cannot replace people’s own accounts, reliable evidence or genuine negotiation.

## Read next

Five of Cups: Compare attending to what is lost and what remains; Four of Swords: Make room to rest while processing disappointment.

sourceRecord.hook: 一句话让你难受了很久。真正需要被说出来的，也许不是「我没事」。

sections.title: 画面没有给这颗心指定主人
paragraphs: 红色的心形悬在灰色背景中央，三柄剑穿过它：中间一柄近乎竖直，另外两柄倾斜交叉。上方和两边是低垂的云，细长雨线向下落。画里没有人物、房屋或正在进行的对话，也没有说明心属于谁。

红心与冷色剑身形成强烈反差，视线几乎没有别的地方可躲。它把受伤的感受画得直接，却没有把伤的原因画出来。三柄剑可以提醒我们观察多个因素，不能据此推导一定有「第三个人」。 [查看本篇实看牌面](https://github.com/guangtoulee/destinypixel/blob/284f7641e41dcaa6685d2d387e31245ca8264d66/public/tarot/rws/three-of-swords.webp)

sections.title: Waite 写的是分离与裂开
paragraphs: Waite 的1911年标注转录列出离开、缺席、延迟、分裂和破裂等意义，并认为图像本身已经相当直接。逆位词表也包含错误、失落和混乱，因此把逆位一律解释为伤口已经愈合，并不符合这份原文。
本文以承认失望、辨认需要来学习此牌，属于现代反思用法。我们保留图像的沉重，但不把历史词表中带有病理化色彩的措辞用来评价任何人的精神状态。 [核对 Waite 单牌原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktsw03.htm)

sections.title: 正位 让感受对应到具体事情
paragraphs: 正位可以表示某个期待受挫，或你终于承认一段安排与自己的需要有距离。先把「很糟」说得更具体：是没有被告知、被误解，还是原先的约定变了？清楚命名会帮助你选择下一步。
承认难受不要求立即宽恕，也不要求马上结束关系。事实、影响、你的需要可以分开处理；有些事能重新协商，有些损失则需要时间慢慢接受。

sections.title: 逆位 观察伤感怎样被处理
paragraphs: 逆位可能是愿意谈及痛处，也可能是反复回想同一句话，始终没有机会澄清。留意你是在逐渐恢复选择，还是逼自己快速翻篇。它不能证明对方已经后悔，修复仍要看现实中的回应与改变。

sections.title: 失望并不只发生在爱情里
paragraphs: 提案没有通过，先区分对作品的反馈与对你整个人的评价。问清被否决的是预算、方向还是表达，能把模糊的挫败变成可处理的部分。
朋友取消了你期待很久的见面，可以直接说失落，再确认是否重新安排。关系里的伤人话语则需要具体讨论「那句话造成什么影响」，而不是用抽到的牌当作指控。离开熟悉的城市时，舍不得也可以与想尝试新生活同时存在。

sections.title: 练习 写一封暂不发送的短信
paragraphs: 用三句话写给让你失望的人或那件事：「发生了什么」「这让我失去了什么」「我现在需要什么」。先放下片刻，再检查有没有把未经证实的动机写成事实；决定是否沟通，可以稍后再做。

sections.title: 三柄剑不是三角关系的证据
paragraphs: 宝剑三不能证明背叛，也不能保证分手。痛苦值得被认真听见，但牌面无法代替当事人的说法、可靠证据或真实协商。
